title: Entrevista geral
summary: As perguntas que aparecem em quase todo processo seletivo: apresentação, motivação, forças e fraquezas, histórias STAR, salário e encerramento.

stages.title: Recrutador
stages.description: Perguntas da primeira conversa, iguais em quase toda empresa.

stages.title: Experiência (STAR)
stages.description: Comportamentais. Tenha 4 ou 5 histórias reais prontas: elas servem para várias perguntas.

stages.title: Como você trabalha
stages.description: Perguntas sobre o seu jeito de trabalhar, aprender e lidar com problemas.

stages.title: Suas perguntas e encerramento
stages.description: Nunca termine sem perguntas. Feche com uma frase curta e positiva.

questions.en: Could you tell me a little bit about yourself?
questions.goal: Seu pitch de 60 a 90 segundos: quem você é profissionalmente e por que faz sentido para a vaga.
questions.answer: Sure! [[I've been working in]] ((your field)) [[for]] ((number of years)). [[I currently work as]] ((your role)) at ((company)), [[where I'm responsible for]] ((two main responsibilities)). [[Prior to that]], ((previous experience in one sentence)). [[What really drives me is]] ((what motivates you)), [[and that's why I'm excited about this role]].
tips: Presente → passado → futuro → ligação com a vaga.
Não conte a vida toda. É um trailer, não o filme.

questions.en: Why do you want to work with us?
questions.goal: Se você pesquisou a empresa e se o interesse é real.
questions.answer: [[I've been following]] ((something specific about the company: product, mission, news)), and [[what caught my attention]] was ((a concrete detail)). [[On top of that]], the role [[is a great match for]] my experience with ((your relevant skill)). [[I believe I can contribute]] from day one.
tips: Cite algo específico da empresa. 'É uma ótima empresa' não conta.

questions.en: Why are you looking for a new opportunity?
questions.goal: Se existe algum problema e se você vai ficar. Querem uma motivação positiva.
questions.answer: [[To be honest]], I'm not running away from anything. I've learned a lot in my current role, but [[I'm looking to]] ((what you want: more ownership, an international team, a bigger product)). [[I believe]] this role is the right next step for that.
tips: Nunca fale mal do emprego atual.

questions.en: What would you say is your greatest strength?
questions.goal: Autoconhecimento. Uma força, com prova.
questions.answer: [[I'd say]] my biggest strength is ((one strength)). [[For instance]], ((a short real example that proves it)). [[That's why]] ((how it helps in this role)).
tips: Uma força só, com um exemplo. Lista de adjetivos não convence.

questions.en: What's your biggest weakness?
questions.goal: Honestidade e maturidade: um ponto real que você já está melhorando.
questions.answer: [[To be honest]], ((a real weakness that doesn't block the job)). [[I've been working on it by]] ((concrete action)), and [[I've already noticed]] ((a real improvement)).
tips: Evite 'sou perfeccionista'. Todo recrutador já ouviu.
Para quem está aprendendo inglês, falar do inglês com o plano de estudo é uma boa resposta.

questions.en: What are your salary expectations?
questions.goal: Se você cabe no orçamento.
questions.answer: Based on my research for similar roles, [[I'm looking for something in the range of]] ((your range, with the currency and period)). [[That said, I'm open to]] discussing the full package. [[Is that within the budget for this role?]]
tips: Pesquise antes. O piso da faixa tem que ser um valor que você aceitaria.

questions.en: When would you be available to start?
questions.goal: Prazo de saída do emprego atual.
questions.answer: I'd need ((notice period)) to hand over my current responsibilities properly, [[so I could start]] ((date)).

questions.en: Can you tell me about a challenging project you worked on?
questions.goal: Como você resolve problemas difíceis. Use STAR.
questions.answer: [[Sure, let me think of a good example.]] [[The situation was that]] ((context)). [[My task was to]] ((your responsibility)). [[What I did was]] ((your actions, in the first person)). [[As a result]], ((measurable result)).
tips: Use 'I' para o que você fez. Termine com um número.

questions.en: Tell me about a time you failed or made a mistake.
questions.goal: Se você assume erros e aprende com eles.
questions.answer: ((A real mistake)). [[To be honest]], it was my fault: ((what went wrong)). I fixed it by ((action)), and [[what I learned was]] ((the lesson and what you do differently now)).

questions.en: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a colleague or your manager.
questions.goal: Se você discorda com respeito e com dados, e depois segue em frente.
questions.answer: ((Situation)). I disagreed because ((reason)). Instead of arguing, I ((how you handled it: data, a proof of concept, a one-on-one conversation)). ((Outcome)). [[Even when the decision doesn't go my way]], once we decide, I fully support it.

questions.en: How do you handle pressure and tight deadlines?
questions.goal: Organização e comunicação.
questions.answer: I [[break the problem down into]] smaller pieces and agree on priorities early. [[I keep people in the loop]]: if something will slip, they hear it from me first. [[For instance]], ((a short real example)).

questions.en: How do you keep your skills up to date?
questions.goal: Curiosidade e autonomia.
questions.answer: [[I'm a big believer in]] learning by doing. [[I usually]] ((how you learn: documentation, courses, newsletters)), but [[what really sticks is]] building things. [[For instance]], ((something you learned recently by building it)).

questions.en: What do you do when you don't know how to solve a problem?
questions.goal: Autonomia sem orgulho: você tenta, pesquisa e pede ajuda na hora certa.
questions.answer: First, I make sure I understand the problem and try to [[narrow it down]]. Then I look at the documentation, the logs and similar issues. [[If I'm still stuck after]] ((a time box, for example an hour)), I ask for help, with what I already tried. [[That way]], nobody wastes time and I still learn.

questions.en: Have you worked remotely before? How do you stay productive?
questions.goal: Para vagas remotas: disciplina e comunicação escrita.
questions.answer: ((Your remote experience)). [[What works for me is]] a fixed routine, clear goals for the day, and over-communicating in writing: short updates, documented decisions. [[I also make sure to]] be available during the team's core hours.

questions.en: Do you have any questions for us?
questions.goal: Nunca responda 'no'. Perguntas boas mostram interesse real.
questions.answer: Yes, a few. [[I'm curious to know]] what the biggest challenge for this team is right now. [[What would success look like]] in the first ninety days? How is the team organized, and who would I work with most closely? And what are the next steps in the process?

questions.en: Great, that's all from our side. Anything else you'd like to add?
questions.goal: Última impressão: curta, positiva, reforçando o encaixe.
questions.answer: Just that I'm really excited about this opportunity. ((One sentence connecting your experience to the role)). [[Thank you for the opportunity]], [[it was great chatting with you]], and [[I look forward to hearing from you]].

title: 70 perguntas frequentes (perfil tech)
summary: As perguntas mais comuns em entrevistas em inglês, do 'tell me about yourself' ao salário, respondidas com a sua trajetória em Python, dados e produto.

stages.title: Abertura e apresentação
stages.description: Os primeiros minutos: inglês, pitch, formação. Aqui se forma a primeira impressão.

stages.title: Experiência e requisitos
stages.description: O que você já fez, o que te falta e por que está saindo. Fatos, não adjetivos.

stages.title: Histórias (STAR)
stages.description: Desafios, falhas e sucessos. Prepare 5 histórias reais e reaproveite: Situation, Task, Action, Result.

stages.title: Carreira e motivação
stages.description: Para onde você vai, por que tecnologia e por que esta empresa.

stages.title: Jeito de trabalhar
stages.description: Rotina, organização, pressão, estresse e mudanças. Querem previsibilidade.

stages.title: Equipe e liderança
stages.description: Colaboração, conflitos, delegar e liderar. Mostre maturidade, nunca reclame de ninguém.

stages.title: Valores e pessoal
stages.description: Perguntas abertas sobre você. Respostas curtas, honestas e que voltem para o trabalho.

stages.title: Condições
stages.description: Horas, viagens, mudança, salário e início. Seja honesto e não feche valor cedo demais.

stages.title: Suas perguntas
stages.description: Sempre tenha perguntas prontas. Elas mostram que você fez a lição de casa.

questions.en: Do you mind if we do this interview in English?
questions.goal: Se você trava ou aceita com tranquilidade. A resposta já é o primeiro teste de inglês.
questions.answer: [[Not at all]], I'd be happy to. I use English every day for documentation and code, [[so it's a great chance to practice]]. [[If I don't understand something, I'll ask you to rephrase it.]]
tips: Sorria e responda rápido. Hesitar aqui passa insegurança.
Já deixe combinado que vai pedir para repetir quando precisar.

questions.en: How would you rate your English?
questions.goal: Se a sua autoavaliação é realista. Exagerar ou se diminuir demais pega mal.
questions.answer: [[I'd say]] my English is ((intermediate to advanced)). Reading and writing are strong, because I work with technical documentation, Stack Overflow and code reviews in English every day. Speaking is [[what I've been working on the most]], ((with daily practice and conversation classes)). [[I can handle]] technical discussions comfortably, and I keep getting better.
tips: Separe as habilidades: leitura, escrita, conversa. Fica mais crível.
Mostre que você está melhorando (o que faz para isso).

questions.en: Tell me a little bit about yourself.
questions.goal: Seu pitch de 60 a 90 segundos: quem você é profissionalmente e por que está aqui.
questions.answer: Sure! I'm Igor, [[I'm a]] software developer and data analyst from Brazil. [[I've been working in]] tech and data [[for]] ((about six years)). [[I currently work as]] a Data Analyst ((at an oil refinery)), [[where I'm responsible for]] Python data pipelines and dashboards built on SAP data. In parallel, I founded PGBA Solutions, [[where I build]] web products end to end with Django, FastAPI, React, TypeScript and PostgreSQL. [[What I enjoy most is]] turning messy data into tools people actually use, [[and that's why this role caught my attention]].
tips: Presente → passado → futuro → ligação com a vaga.
Ensaie até sair sem ler. Grave no celular e ouça.
Não fale de família, idade ou hobbies aqui, a não ser que perguntem.
follow_ups: Which technology do you use the most?

questions.en: What's your background?
questions.goal: Formação e caminho até a tecnologia. Querem entender a sua história em ordem.
questions.answer: [[My background is in]] ((your degree)). [[I started my career in]] ((first area)), and [[that's where I discovered]] programming: I started automating reports with Python and never stopped. [[Since then]], I've moved more and more into software development: first data pipelines and dashboards, and later full web applications at my own company.
tips: Conte como uma linha do tempo curta, com uma virada clara.

questions.en: What did you graduate in?
questions.goal: Pergunta direta. Responda o curso, a instituição e o ano, e ligue com o seu trabalho.
questions.answer: [[I graduated in]] ((your course)) [[from]] ((university)) [[in]] ((year)). [[On top of that]], I've taken courses in ((Python, data engineering, cloud)), because most of what I use today I learned by building real projects.
tips: Se a formação não for em computação, mostre o que estudou depois.

questions.en: What tools and technologies are you most experienced with?
questions.goal: A versão de tecnologia do 'você sabe Excel?'. Querem saber o que você domina de verdade.
questions.answer: [[My main stack is]] Python: pandas for data, Django and FastAPI for backends. On the frontend, React with TypeScript. For databases, mostly PostgreSQL, and I write a lot of SQL. [[I'm also comfortable with]] Git, Docker, Power BI and of course Excel, which is everywhere at the refinery. [[I'm less experienced with]] ((a tool from the job description)), but I pick up new tools quickly.
tips: Separe o que você domina do que já usou. Nunca liste o que não sustenta.

questions.en: Do you have any experience dealing with clients or sales?
questions.goal: Comunicação com cliente e visão de negócio, importante para quem tem empresa própria.
questions.answer: Yes, through PGBA. [[As a founder, I've been the one]] talking to clients, understanding their problem, writing proposals and negotiating scope. [[It taught me to]] explain technical decisions in business terms, which helps a lot when working with product people.
tips: Transforme a PGBA em prova de comunicação e de visão de produto.

questions.en: After reading the job description, do you think you meet all the requirements? Which ones would you need to improve?
questions.goal: Honestidade e autoconhecimento. Ninguém cumpre 100%; querem ver como você fecha a lacuna.
questions.answer: [[I meet most of them]]: Python, APIs, SQL and working with data from different sources are things I do every day. [[Where I'd need to ramp up is]] ((one requirement, e.g. Kubernetes)). [[What I'm doing about it is]] ((a course or side project)), and [[I've done that before]]: I learned FastAPI by shipping a real project with it.
tips: Cite uma lacuna real e o que você já está fazendo para fechá-la.
Nunca diga 'I have all of them' sem poder provar.

questions.en: Do you have a work visa, or would you need sponsorship?
questions.goal: Questão prática para vagas no exterior. Para vagas remotas, explique como funciona.
questions.answer: ((For remote roles:)) I'd work remotely from Brazil as a contractor, [[so I wouldn't need a visa]]. ((If the role is on-site: I don't have a visa yet, so I'd need sponsorship / I have a ... visa.))
tips: Responda direto. Se precisar de patrocínio, diga sem rodeios.

questions.en: Why do you want to leave your current job?
questions.goal: Se há problema (conflito, demissão) e se você vai ficar. Querem uma motivação positiva.
questions.answer: [[To be honest]], I'm not running away from anything. I've learned a lot at the refinery, but data analysis is only part of what I want to do. [[I'm looking to]] work full-time on software products, with a strong engineering team and in an international environment. [[This role is the natural next step for that.]]
tips: Fale do que você busca, nunca do que você quer evitar.

questions.en: Why did you leave your last job?
questions.goal: Igual à anterior, mas sobre o passado. Uma frase clara e positiva basta.
questions.answer: ((I left ... because ...)). [[It was a good place to learn]], but [[I wanted to]] ((grow / work more with code / take on more responsibility)), and the move to ((next job)) gave me exactly that.
tips: Se foi demitido, diga com calma, em uma frase, e foque no que aprendeu.

questions.en: What are your main responsibilities in your current position?
questions.goal: O dia a dia real e o tamanho do seu escopo. Verbos de ação e resultados.
questions.answer: At the refinery, [[I'm responsible for]] three main things. First, building Python pipelines that extract and clean data from SAP and spreadsheets. Second, creating dashboards that ((operations / management)) use to make decisions. Third, automating manual reports, which ((saved the team X hours a week)). At PGBA, [[I own the whole cycle]]: from the first conversation with the client to deploying and maintaining the product.
tips: Três responsabilidades com verbos fortes: build, automate, own.

questions.en: Have you ever had to let someone go? How did you feel about it?
questions.goal: Maturidade em decisões difíceis. Se nunca aconteceu, diga e mostre como faria.
questions.answer: ((If yes: At PGBA, I had to end a contract with a freelancer who ... It wasn't easy, but ...)). ((If no:)) [[I haven't had to do that so far]], but I've given difficult feedback. [[I believe]] the key is to be clear early, so it's never a surprise, and to treat the person with respect.

questions.en: Tell me about a time you faced a completely new task. How did you deal with it? What was the outcome?
questions.goal: Como você aprende sob demanda. A melhor resposta mostra método, não sorte.
questions.answer: [[The situation was that]] ((a PGBA client needed a feature with a technology I had never used, e.g. payments / maps / FastAPI)). [[My task was to]] deliver it in ((two weeks)). [[What I did was]] read the official docs first, build a tiny proof of concept, and only then plug it into the product, with tests around it. [[As a result]], ((we delivered on time and the client ...)). [[What I learned was]] that a small prototype saves a lot of time.
tips: Mostre o método: estudar, prototipar, integrar, testar.

questions.en: What was your biggest failure at work, and what did you learn from it?
questions.goal: Autocrítica. Fugir da pergunta ('sou perfeccionista') é a pior resposta.
questions.answer: ((A real failure: e.g. I underestimated a PGBA project and missed the deadline by three weeks)). [[To be honest]], it was my fault: ((I didn't break the scope down)). I told the client early, renegotiated the scope and delivered the most important part first. [[What I learned was]] to split work into small deliveries and estimate with a margin. [[Since then]], ((what you do differently)).
tips: Escolha um erro real, já resolvido, e gaste mais tempo no aprendizado.

questions.en: Tell me something you didn't like about your last job.
questions.goal: Armadilha: querem ver se você fala mal da empresa. Escolha algo neutro e construtivo.
questions.answer: [[If I had to pick one thing]], it would be the amount of manual work in some processes, like reports built by hand every week. [[But instead of just complaining]], I automated a few of them with Python, [[and that's actually how]] I got more involved with software.
tips: Nunca critique pessoas. Critique um processo e mostre o que você fez.

questions.en: Describe the biggest challenge you've had at work and how you handled it.
questions.goal: Sua história técnica mais forte, em formato STAR.
questions.answer: [[The biggest challenge was]] ((consolidating data from SAP and dozens of spreadsheets into one reliable dataset)). The same items had different names, codes and formats. [[What I did was]] build a Python pipeline that standardized the fields, removed duplicates, and flagged bad records for review instead of silently fixing them. [[As a result]], ((the monthly report went from X days to Y hours)), and people started trusting the numbers.
tips: Tenha números reais. Sem números a história perde metade da força.

questions.en: Give me an example of something you did really well at work.
questions.goal: Um resultado concreto e o seu papel nele.
questions.answer: [[One thing I'm proud of is]] ((an automation at the refinery)). Every week, ((someone spent a whole day)) copying data into a report. I built a script that did it in ((minutes)) and added checks to catch inconsistent data. [[It saved the team]] ((hours per month)), and [[it ended up being used by]] ((other areas)).

questions.en: What are the most successful projects you've worked on?
questions.goal: Projetos com impacto. Escolha um ou dois e conte o problema, a solução e o resultado.
questions.answer: [[I'd highlight two]]. The first is ((a PGBA product)): a web platform with a Django or FastAPI backend, React frontend and PostgreSQL, [[that's now used by]] ((N users / clients)). [[I designed it end to end]], from the data model to the deploy. The second is ((the data pipeline at the refinery)), which ((result)). [[Both of them taught me]] to always start from the user's problem.
follow_ups: What was the hardest technical decision in that project?
What would you do differently today?

questions.en: What's important to you in a company?
questions.goal: Se os seus valores combinam com os deles.
questions.answer: [[For me, the most important thing is]] a team that cares about quality: code reviews, tests and honest feedback. [[I also value]] autonomy with clear goals, and a culture where it's okay to ask questions. [[That's the kind of place where]] I do my best work.
tips: Pesquise os valores da empresa e cite um que combine com o seu.

questions.en: Why would you like to work for us? What do you know about our company?
questions.goal: Se você pesquisou. Resposta genérica elimina candidatos.
questions.answer: [[I've been reading about]] ((the company: product, mission, recent news)), and [[what caught my attention]] was ((a concrete detail)). [[On top of that]], the role [[is a great match for]] my experience with ((Python / data / APIs)). [[I believe I could contribute]] to ((a specific challenge)) from the beginning.
tips: Leia o site, o LinkedIn, o blog técnico e o GitHub da empresa antes.
Cite produto, clientes ou stack. 'É uma ótima empresa' não conta.

questions.en: Are you applying for other jobs?
questions.goal: Urgência e concorrência. Não precisa dar nomes.
questions.answer: ((Answer honestly: 'Yes, I'm in early conversations with a couple of companies' or 'Not actively')). [[But this role is at the top of my list]], because it matches what I do best.

questions.en: What are you looking for in a job?
questions.goal: Se o que você quer existe nesta vaga.
questions.answer: [[I'm looking for]] three things: challenging technical problems, especially with data and APIs; a strong team I can learn from; and real ownership, being involved from the idea to production. [[From what I've seen]], this role has all three.

questions.en: What courses or skills are you planning to study next?
questions.goal: Se você investe na própria carreira e se o plano faz sentido para a vaga.
questions.answer: [[Right now I'm focused on]] two things: my spoken English, ((with daily practice)), and ((cloud: an AWS or Azure certification)). [[Next, I'd like to]] go deeper into ((system design / data engineering)), because it's where I see the biggest impact in the kind of products I build.
tips: Cite algo que você já começou. Plano sem ação não convence.

questions.en: What are your short-term and long-term career goals?
questions.goal: Se você tem direção e se ela cabe na empresa.
questions.answer: [[In the short term]], [[I want to]] join a strong engineering team, deliver well and become a reference in ((Python and data)). [[In the long term]], [[I see myself]] as a senior or staff engineer, designing systems and helping other developers grow.

questions.en: Where do you see yourself in five years?
questions.goal: Ambição realista e se você pretende ficar.
questions.answer: [[In five years, I see myself]] as a senior engineer who owns important parts of the product, and [[ideally]] still at this company, growing with it. I'd like to be the person people come to for ((data and backend)) questions, and [[to be mentoring]] newer developers.
tips: Não diga que quer abrir a sua empresa ou o cargo do entrevistador.

questions.en: Are you satisfied with your career so far?
questions.goal: Equilíbrio: orgulho do caminho e vontade de crescer.
questions.answer: [[Overall, yes]]. I built a solid base in data and I've shipped real products at PGBA. [[But I'm not done]]: the next step is working on larger products with a bigger team, [[which is exactly why I'm here]].

questions.en: Why did you choose a career in technology?
questions.goal: A motivação real. Uma história curta e verdadeira vale mais que um discurso.
questions.answer: [[It started when]] ((I automated my first report with Python)). Seeing a task that took a day run in seconds was addictive. [[What keeps me here is]] that every problem is different, and I'm always learning. I like that software has a real, visible impact on people's work.

questions.en: How do you keep improving professionally? Are you seeing results?
questions.goal: Disciplina de aprendizado contínuo, com provas.
questions.answer: [[I learn mostly by building]]. Every new PGBA project is a chance to try something, like ((FastAPI or TypeScript)). [[On top of that]], I read documentation and engineering blogs, and ((take courses)). [[And yes, I'm seeing results]]: ((one concrete result, e.g. I moved from scripts to full web applications in two years)).

questions.en: Do you consider yourself successful?
questions.goal: Autoconfiança sem arrogância.
questions.answer: [[In many ways, yes]]. I built a career in tech, founded a company, and my work is used by real people every day. [[But for me, success is a direction, not a destination]]: I still have a lot to learn.

questions.en: What's your dream job?
questions.goal: Se a vaga se aproxima do que você quer. Descreva características, não um cargo em outra empresa.
questions.answer: [[My dream job is]] one where I solve real problems with data and code, on a product people depend on, with a team that pushes me to be better. [[Honestly, this role is very close to that.]]

questions.en: What's your typical work routine? How do you organize yourself?
questions.goal: Organização e previsibilidade, ainda mais em trabalho remoto.
questions.answer: [[I usually start the day by]] checking messages and reviewing my priorities. [[Then I block]] the morning for focused work, like coding or data analysis, with notifications off. Meetings and code reviews go to the afternoon. I track tasks in ((Trello / Jira / Notion)), and at the end of the day [[I write down]] where I stopped, so the next day starts fast.

questions.en: You do many different tasks at work. Which one do you like the most?
questions.goal: O que te dá energia. Ideal se coincidir com o centro da vaga.
questions.answer: [[What I enjoy the most is]] designing the solution: modeling the data, deciding how the API should look, and then seeing it work end to end. [[I also really like]] debugging hard problems. Finding the root cause is very satisfying.

questions.en: Do you find any work activities boring?
questions.goal: Armadilha: querem ver se você evita trabalho necessário.
questions.answer: [[Every job has repetitive tasks]], like filling in reports or manual checks. [[But I see them as]] candidates for automation. Many of my best scripts started because something was boring. [[And when it can't be automated]], I just do it well and move on.

questions.en: What kind of work environment are you most comfortable in?
questions.goal: Encaixe com a cultura (remoto, ritmo, autonomia).
questions.answer: [[I'm most comfortable in]] an environment with clear goals and autonomy to reach them. I've been working remotely ((for years)), so [[I'm used to]] written communication and async work. [[I also like]] teams where people share knowledge openly.

questions.en: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
questions.goal: Autoconhecimento. Uma força com prova e uma fraqueza real com plano.
questions.answer: [[I'd say my main strength is]] turning messy problems into working solutions. [[For instance]], ((the SAP data pipeline)). [[As for weaknesses]], I sometimes try to solve everything myself before asking for help, probably because of years running my own company. [[I've been working on that]] by setting a time limit: if I'm stuck for ((an hour)), I ask.
tips: A fraqueza tem que ser real e não pode ser essencial para a vaga.

questions.en: How would you describe your current or previous boss?
questions.goal: Armadilha: nunca fale mal. Querem ver como você se relaciona com a hierarquia.
questions.answer: ((My manager)) [[is very results-oriented]] and gives me a lot of autonomy. [[What I learned from them is]] ((to always connect the data to a business decision)). [[We have a good relationship]], with honest feedback in both directions.
tips: Mesmo que o chefe seja ruim, fale de algo que você aprendeu.

questions.en: How would your boss and coworkers describe you?
questions.goal: Como você é visto. Use palavras que outras pessoas realmente usaram.
questions.answer: [[I think they'd say]] I'm reliable and the person who gets things done. ((In my last feedback, my manager said ...)). [[My coworkers would probably add that]] I'm always willing to help, especially with Python and data problems.
tips: Se tiver um feedback real ou recomendação no LinkedIn, cite.

questions.en: Do you consider yourself a workaholic?
questions.goal: Comprometimento x equilíbrio. O ideal é o meio-termo.
questions.answer: [[Not really]]. I'm very committed, and when there's an urgent issue I stay until it's solved. [[But I believe]] rest is part of doing good work: a tired developer writes bugs. [[So I try to keep]] a healthy balance.

questions.en: How do you work under pressure?
questions.goal: Se você mantém a qualidade e a comunicação quando aperta.
questions.answer: [[I stay calm and get organized]]. I break the problem into smaller pieces, [[deal with the most critical part first]], and keep people updated. [[For example]], ((a production issue at PGBA with a client waiting)): ((what you did)). [[Pressure actually helps me focus]].

questions.en: How do you handle stress?
questions.goal: Se você tem estratégias saudáveis.
questions.answer: At work, [[I handle stress by]] organizing: writing everything down and talking to the team early when something is at risk. Outside work, ((exercise / time with family)) [[helps me recharge]].

questions.en: How do you deal with change at work?
questions.goal: Adaptabilidade. Tecnologia muda o tempo todo.
questions.answer: [[I see change as part of the job]], especially in tech. [[When priorities change]], I try to understand the reason behind the decision, and then adapt quickly. [[At PGBA, for example]], ((a client changed the scope mid-project, and ...)).

questions.en: Can you think outside the box?
questions.goal: Criatividade com exemplo, não só 'sim'.
questions.answer: [[I'd like to think so]]. [[For example]], ((instead of building a full system for a client, I suggested a simple spreadsheet integration that solved 80% of the problem in a week)). [[Sometimes the creative solution is the simplest one.]]

questions.en: In your opinion, what are the hardest decisions to make?
questions.goal: Como você raciocina sobre trade-offs.
questions.answer: [[For me, the hardest decisions are]] the ones with trade-offs and incomplete information, like ((shipping now with technical debt or delaying to do it right)). [[What helps me is]] making the trade-offs explicit, talking to the people affected, and choosing an option that's easy to revisit.

questions.en: How has the way you work changed after the pandemic?
questions.goal: Adaptação ao trabalho remoto e híbrido.
questions.answer: [[The biggest change was]] remote work. [[I learned to]] communicate much more in writing, document decisions and work with people in different places. [[It also showed me]] that I'm very productive working remotely, ((which is why I'm looking for remote roles)).

questions.en: Are you a team player?
questions.goal: Colaboração com exemplo concreto.
questions.answer: Yes. [[I enjoy working with others]], and I think software is a team sport: code reviews, pair programming and sharing knowledge make the product better. [[For example]], ((I created a small Python guide for my team at the refinery so they could run the reports themselves)).

questions.en: Are you able to delegate work?
questions.goal: Confiança nos outros e capacidade de não centralizar.
questions.answer: Yes, [[I've learned to]], mostly at PGBA. At first I tried to do everything myself, [[but that doesn't scale]]. Now I give context, define what 'done' looks like, and stay available for questions, [[without micromanaging]].

questions.en: Are you able to make decisions on your own?
questions.goal: Autonomia com responsabilidade.
questions.answer: Yes. [[Running my own company taught me to]] make decisions with the information I have. [[For small, reversible decisions]], I decide and move on. [[For big ones]], like architecture or anything that affects clients, I gather input first and document the reasons.

questions.en: Are you more of a leader or a follower?
questions.goal: Flexibilidade. A melhor resposta: depende do contexto.
questions.answer: [[It depends on the situation]]. When I know the subject well, like data pipelines, [[I naturally take the lead]]. When someone else has more experience, [[I'm happy to follow]] and learn. [[What matters is]] that the team delivers.

questions.en: Do you usually lead people at work? How do you get along with them?
questions.goal: Experiência real de liderança, mesmo informal.
questions.answer: ((At PGBA, I coordinate freelancers / a small team)). [[I try to lead by example]]: being clear about priorities and reviewing work with respect. [[We get along well]], because I listen and I give credit to the people who did the work.

questions.en: Do you consider yourself a good leader?
questions.goal: Humildade com evidência.
questions.answer: [[I'm still learning]], but I think I have good foundations: I communicate clearly, I'm fair, and I care about people growing. ((The freelancers I've worked with keep coming back to work with me)), [[which I take as a good sign]].

questions.en: What qualities make a good leader?
questions.goal: Sua visão de liderança.
questions.answer: [[In my opinion]], a good leader gives clear direction, removes obstacles for the team, and is honest, even when the news is bad. [[Above all]], a good leader makes other people better. [[In tech]], that also means protecting the team's time to focus.

questions.en: What irritates you about coworkers?
questions.goal: Armadilha: não reclame. Mostre como você lida com o incômodo.
questions.answer: [[I don't get irritated easily]]. [[If I had to pick something]], it would be when problems are hidden until it's too late. [[When that happens]], I talk to the person directly and privately, because usually there's a reason behind it.

questions.en: Have you ever had problems with someone at work?
questions.goal: Maturidade. Ninguém se dá bem com todos; mostre como resolveu.
questions.answer: [[Nothing serious]], but I've had misunderstandings. ((Once, a colleague and I had different expectations about a deadline)). [[We talked it through]], agreed on priorities, [[and since then]] we write down what we agree on.

questions.en: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a coworker or a manager. How did you handle it?
questions.goal: Discordar com respeito e com dados, e depois seguir em frente.
questions.answer: ((Situation: a manager wanted to keep updating a report by hand / a colleague wanted to use a different database)). I disagreed because ((reason)). [[Instead of arguing]], I prepared a small comparison with data, [[and we decided together]]. ((Outcome)). [[Even when the decision doesn't go my way]], once it's made, I fully support it.
tips: Nunca conte uma história em que o outro era incompetente.

questions.en: What do you like to do in your free time?
questions.goal: Quem você é fora do trabalho. Curto e verdadeiro.
questions.answer: [[In my free time, I like to]] ((spend time with family / exercise / travel)). [[I also enjoy]] building small side projects, like ((this app to study English with chunks, written in Python and React)).
tips: Este próprio app é um ótimo exemplo de projeto pessoal: cite!

questions.en: What motivates you?
questions.goal: O que te faz render. Ideal se combinar com a vaga.
questions.answer: [[What motivates me most is]] seeing people use something I built. When a report that took a day runs in seconds, or a client tells me the product changed their routine, [[that's what keeps me going]]. [[I'm also motivated by]] learning.

questions.en: What's more important to you: money or the work itself?
questions.goal: Equilíbrio. Dizer só 'dinheiro' ou só 'trabalho' soa falso.
questions.answer: [[Both matter, to be honest]]. Fair pay lets me focus on the work without worrying. [[But money alone wouldn't keep me]] in a job where I'm not learning or making an impact. [[The work itself is what keeps me engaged]].

questions.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?
questions.goal: Pergunta descontraída: querem ver se você trabalharia mesmo sem precisar.
questions.answer: [[First, I'd take care of my family]]. [[But I wouldn't stop working]]: I'd probably keep building software, maybe ((tools for education)), because I really enjoy it.

questions.en: What's your view on the current economic situation in Brazil?
questions.goal: Pensamento crítico sem polêmica. Evite política partidária.
questions.answer: [[It's a challenging moment]], ((brief, neutral comment)). [[What I see in tech is that]] Brazilian developers are working more and more for international companies, [[which is a great opportunity]] for both sides: companies get talent in a close time zone, and we grow professionally.
tips: Fique no neutro e volte para o trabalho remoto/internacional.

questions.en: Why should we hire you?
questions.goal: Seu argumento de venda final: 3 motivos ligados à vaga.
questions.answer: [[I'd say three reasons]]. First, I have hands-on experience with exactly what this role needs: ((Python, APIs, SQL and messy data)). Second, I've owned products end to end at PGBA, so [[I don't need someone to tell me every step]]. Third, [[I learn fast]] and I care about quality. [[I'm confident I can deliver results quickly here]].
tips: Ligue cada motivo a um requisito da descrição da vaga.

questions.en: Is there anything that's not on your resume that you'd like to mention?
questions.goal: Chance de mostrar algo extra que te diferencia.
questions.answer: [[Actually, yes]]. I've been building ((this English-learning app)) as a side project: the same library runs in Python and in a React and TypeScript web app, with tests checking that both generate exactly the same output. [[It shows how I like to work]]: small, tested pieces that I can reuse.

questions.en: How long would you expect to stay with us if hired?
questions.goal: Se você vai sair em seis meses.
questions.answer: [[I'm looking for a long-term position]]. [[As long as]] I keep learning and contributing, I see myself here for many years.

questions.en: How many hours a week did you usually work in your previous job?
questions.goal: Ritmo de trabalho e expectativas.
questions.answer: ((Usually forty hours a week)). [[When there was a deadline or an incident]], I worked longer, but that was the exception, not the rule.

questions.en: Are you willing to work overtime, nights or weekends?
questions.goal: Disponibilidade. Seja honesto sobre limites.
questions.answer: [[When it's really necessary]], like a production incident or a critical release, [[I don't see a problem with that]]. [[I just think]] it shouldn't become the routine, because good planning prevents most of it.

questions.en: Do you mind traveling on business?
questions.goal: Disponibilidade para viagens (ex.: encontros do time remoto).
questions.answer: [[Not at all]]. [[I'd actually enjoy]] meeting the team in person from time to time, ((as long as I have some notice to organize things at home)).

questions.en: Would you be willing to relocate?
questions.goal: Flexibilidade. Se não puder, diga, mas sem fechar a porta de cara.
questions.answer: ((Decide before the interview.)) [[I'm open to discussing it]] if it makes sense for both sides. [[That said]], I'm fully set up to work remotely and ((I'd prefer a remote role)).

questions.en: What are your salary expectations?
questions.goal: Se você cabe no orçamento. Evite dar um número antes de saber a faixa.
questions.answer: [[Could you share the salary range for this position?]] ((If they insist:)) Based on my research for this kind of role, [[I'm looking for something in the range of]] ((X to Y per month)). [[That said, I'm open to]] discussing the full package.
tips: Primeiro pergunte a faixa. Se insistirem, dê uma faixa, nunca um número só.
Para vagas internacionais, pense em dólares por mês e lembre que contractor não tem 13º, férias pagas nem FGTS.

questions.en: Can you start immediately?
questions.goal: Prazo real. Sair do jeito certo do emprego atual é bem visto.
questions.answer: I'd need ((two weeks / thirty days)) to hand over my current responsibilities properly. [[I want to leave in a good way]], [[just like I'd do here]]. [[So I could start]] ((around date)).

questions.en: Do you have any questions for us?
questions.goal: Nunca diga 'no'. Perguntas mostram interesse e ajudam você a decidir.
questions.answer: [[Yes, I do, thank you.]] [[What are the main challenges]] the team is facing right now?
tips: Leve 3 ou 4 perguntas anotadas. Use as próximas como ideias.
Não pergunte de salário e benefícios na primeira conversa com o técnico.

questions.en: (You ask) Is this a new position, or are you replacing someone?
questions.goal: Entender o contexto da vaga: crescimento ou reposição.
questions.answer: [[I was wondering]], is this a new position, [[or is it a replacement]]?

questions.en: (You ask) Who would I be reporting to?
questions.goal: Saber quem é o seu gestor e como o time se organiza.
questions.answer: [[Who would I be reporting to]], and how is the team structured?

questions.en: (You ask) What would success look like in the first three months?
questions.goal: A melhor pergunta para vagas de tecnologia: mostra foco em resultado.
questions.answer: [[What would success look like]] for this role in the first three months?

questions.en: (You ask) What does the development process look like?
questions.goal: Como o time trabalha: deploy, revisão, testes, sprints.
questions.answer: [[Could you tell me a bit about]] the development process? For example, how code reviews, testing and deploys work.

questions.en: (You ask) What are the working hours? Is overtime common?
questions.goal: Rotina real, sobretudo em fusos diferentes.
questions.answer: [[What are the usual working hours]] for the team, and which time zone are most people in?

questions.en: (You ask) What are the next steps in the process?
questions.goal: Fechar a conversa sabendo o que vem depois.
questions.answer: [[Thank you for your time.]] [[What are the next steps]] in the process?
tips: Termine com uma frase positiva: 'I'm really excited about this opportunity.'

title: Senior Software Engineer, Vendor Data Platform
summary: Plataforma que limpa, cruza e unifica dados de fornecedores de vários clientes e entrega para produtos de pagamento via API. Python, TypeScript, SQL, Azure/AWS, eventos.

stages.title: Recrutador
stages.description: Primeira conversa com a DistantJob: trajetória, motivação, inglês, horário, salário e disponibilidade. Eles filtram encaixe e comunicação, não código.

stages.title: Experiência (STAR)
stages.description: Perguntas comportamentais. Responda sempre com uma história real: Situation, Task, Action, Result.

stages.title: Técnica
stages.description: Python, APIs, SQL, multi-tenant, eventos, nuvem, frontend e testes.

stages.title: Dados de fornecedores
stages.description: O coração da vaga: matching, deduplicação, reconciliação e qualidade de dados num contexto de pagamentos.

stages.title: System design
stages.description: Desenhar a plataforma no quadro: ingestão, processamento, armazenamento, API e escala.

stages.title: Suas perguntas e encerramento
stages.description: Perguntar bem mostra senioridade. Tenha 3 ou 4 perguntas prontas.

questions.en: So, Igor, could you walk me through your background?
questions.goal: Seu pitch de 90 segundos. Querem ver se você se comunica bem em inglês e se a sua história leva naturalmente até esta vaga.
questions.answer: Sure! [[I've been working in]] tech and data [[for]] ((about six years)). [[I currently work as]] a Data Analyst ((at an oil refinery in Brazil)), [[where I'm responsible for]] building data pipelines and dashboards with Python. In parallel, I founded PGBA Solutions, [[where I've been hands-on with]] the whole stack: Python backends with Django and FastAPI, React and TypeScript frontends, PostgreSQL, and integrations with third-party APIs. A lot of my work is exactly what this role describes: taking data from different sources, cleaning it, matching records and exposing them through APIs. [[I'm now looking to]] focus that experience on one product with a strong engineering team, [[and that's what brought me here today]].
tips: Estrutura: presente → passado → futuro → ligação com a vaga. No máximo 90 segundos.
Ensaie em voz alta até sair sem ler. Grave no celular e ouça.
Termine falando da vaga, assim a próxima pergunta vem para o seu terreno.
follow_ups: How many years have you worked professionally with Python?

questions.en: What caught your attention about this role?
questions.goal: Se você leu a descrição e se o seu interesse é real (não só 'qualquer vaga remota').
questions.answer: Two things. First, the problem itself. [[Turning messy data into]] clean, trustworthy records is the kind of work I enjoy most, and I deal with it every day ((with SAP and spreadsheet data at the refinery)). Second, the ownership. The description says this is not a 'pick up tickets' role, [[and that's exactly what I'm looking for]]: being involved from the first scoping conversation all the way to production.
tips: Cite algo específico da descrição: 'garbage in, garbage out', ownership, matching.

questions.en: Why are you looking for a new opportunity right now?
questions.goal: Se há algum problema (conflito, demissão) e se você vai ficar. Querem uma motivação positiva.
questions.answer: [[To be honest]], I'm not running away from anything. I've learned a lot in my current role, but [[I'm looking to]] work on a software product at scale, with a strong engineering team and in an international environment. [[I believe]] this role is the right next step for that.
tips: Nunca fale mal do emprego atual.
Fale do que você busca, não do que você quer evitar.

questions.en: You run your own company. How would that work with a full-time position?
questions.goal: PERGUNTA QUASE CERTA. A DistantJob contrata em tempo integral e exclusivo (8h/dia). Querem ter certeza de que a PGBA não vai competir com o trabalho.
questions.answer: [[That's a fair question.]] ((Decida antes e diga a verdade: por exemplo, 'PGBA would be on hold' / 'my partner would run the day-to-day' / 'I'd only keep it outside working hours, with no conflict of interest')). [[To be clear]], this position would be my main focus: full-time, eight hours a day, aligned with US business hours.
tips: Decida a resposta real ANTES da entrevista. Hesitar aqui pesa muito.
Transforme a PGBA em ponto forte: é onde você teve ownership de ponta a ponta.

questions.en: This role requires overlap with US business hours. Does that work for you?
questions.goal: Confirmação prática de disponibilidade.
questions.answer: Yes, [[I'm fully comfortable with that]]. Brazil is usually one or two hours ahead of US Eastern time, depending on daylight saving, [[so I could easily work]] ((from 10 AM to 7 PM Brasília time)). If the team is on the West Coast, I can shift my day later.
tips: Brasília (UTC-3) fica 2h à frente de Nova York no inverno de lá e 1h no verão de lá.
Pergunte de volta: 'Which time zone is the team in?'

questions.en: When would you be available to start?
questions.goal: Prazo de aviso prévio e quando você realmente pode começar.
questions.answer: I'd need ((two weeks / thirty days)) to hand over my current responsibilities properly, [[so I could start]] ((around date)).
tips: Sair do jeito certo do emprego atual é bem visto. Não prometa 'amanhã'.

questions.en: What are your salary expectations?
questions.goal: Se você cabe no orçamento. A DistantJob costuma pagar em dólar, por mês, como contractor.
questions.answer: Based on my research for senior remote roles with this scope, [[I'm looking for something in the range of]] ((X to Y US dollars per month)). [[That said, I'm open to]] discussing the full package. [[Is that within the budget for this role?]]
tips: Responda em dólares por MÊS (é como a DistantJob costuma falar).
Pesquise antes. O piso da faixa tem que ser um valor que você aceitaria.
Contractor não tem 13º, férias pagas nem FGTS: considere isso no valor.

questions.en: The position is as an independent contractor. Are you comfortable with that?
questions.goal: Se você sabe emitir nota/fatura para o exterior e receber em dólar.
questions.answer: Yes. ((I already have a company / CNPJ)), so invoicing an international client and receiving in US dollars [[won't be a problem]].
tips: Confirme com seu contador como faturar exportação de serviços antes da conversa.

questions.en: How comfortable are you working in English day to day?
questions.goal: Se você vai conseguir participar de reuniões, code reviews e Slack com o time americano.
questions.answer: I read and write in English every day: documentation, code, technical discussions. Speaking is the skill [[I've been actively improving]], ((with daily practice)). In technical conversations I'm comfortable, and [[if I don't understand something, I ask]] instead of assuming. I think that matters more than a perfect accent.
tips: Seja honesto. A própria entrevista já é o teste.
Se não entender uma pergunta: 'Sorry, could you rephrase that?'

questions.en: Are you interviewing with other companies at the moment?
questions.goal: Urgência e concorrência. Não precisa dar nomes.
questions.answer: ((Answer honestly: 'I'm in early conversations with a couple of companies' or 'Not actively')), but this role is [[at the top of my list]] because it matches what I do best.

questions.en: Tell me about a project you owned from design to production.
questions.goal: Ownership real. Querem ouvir decisões que VOCÊ tomou, não só tarefas que executou.
questions.answer: [[Sure, let me think of a good example.]] At PGBA, ((we built a SaaS for ...)). [[The situation was that]] ((the client had ... problem)). [[My task was to]] design and build it end to end. [[What I did was]] ((define the data model in PostgreSQL, build the API with Django/FastAPI, the React frontend, set up deploy and monitoring)). [[As a result]], ((numbers: users, time saved, revenue)). [[What I learned was]] ((one real lesson)).
tips: Use 'I' para o que você fez. 'We' só para o contexto do time.
Tenha números: usuários, tempo, custo, erros. Sem números a história perde força.
follow_ups: What would you do differently today?
What was the hardest technical decision?

questions.en: Tell me about a time you had to deal with messy data from multiple sources.
questions.goal: Experiência direta com o problema da vaga.
questions.answer: [[The situation was that]] ((we were pulling data from SAP and spreadsheets)), and the same entity appeared with different names, formats and duplicates. [[My task was to]] build one reliable dataset for ((reporting)). [[What I did was]] create a Python pipeline that first standardized the fields, then deduplicated using ((the key you used)), and added validation checks that flagged bad records instead of silently fixing them. [[As a result]], ((the report went from X days to Y hours / errors dropped by Z%)).
tips: Esta é a sua melhor história para esta vaga: prepare-a com detalhes reais.
Na mensagem ao recrutador você disse que lida com matching e deduplicação multi-tenant. Tenha um exemplo concreto que sustente isso.

questions.en: Tell me about a production issue you were responsible for. What happened?
questions.goal: Como você age sob pressão e se aprende com o erro (postmortem).
questions.answer: [[We ran into]] a major performance issue ((at PGBA)): ((some pages took over ten seconds)). [[What I did was]] [[dive deep into]] the PostgreSQL logs and query plans. [[It turned out to be]] missing indexes and N+1 queries in the Django ORM. I added the indexes, fixed the queries with select_related and prefetch_related, and added a test that fails if the number of queries grows. [[As a result]], ((response time dropped from X to Y)). After that, [[I made sure to]] monitor slow queries in production.
tips: Confirme os números reais. Termine sempre com o que mudou para não repetir.

questions.en: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision.
questions.goal: Se você sabe discordar com respeito e com dados, e depois seguir em frente.
questions.answer: ((Situation)). I disagreed because ((reason)). Instead of arguing in the meeting, I wrote down the trade-offs and built a small proof of concept to compare both options. ((Outcome: we went with X)). Even when the decision doesn't go my way, [[I'm a big believer in]] 'disagree and commit': once we decide, I fully support it.
tips: Nunca conte uma história em que o outro era 'burro'. Mostre respeito.

questions.en: Tell me about a mistake you made and what you learned from it.
questions.goal: Autocrítica e maturidade. Fugir da pergunta é a pior resposta.
questions.answer: ((A real mistake: e.g. I ran a database migration that locked a large table in production)). [[To be honest]], it was my fault: ((what went wrong)). I fixed it by ((action)) and communicated clearly with ((the client / team)). [[What I learned was]] ((to test migrations with production-sized data and keep them backwards compatible)).
tips: Escolha um erro real, já resolvido, e foque no aprendizado.

questions.en: How do you work with product when the requirements are unclear?
questions.goal: A vaga diz 'partner closely with product'. Querem autonomia sem sair construindo a coisa errada.
questions.answer: First, I ask questions to understand the problem behind the request: who is the user and [[what does success look like]]. Then I write down my assumptions and [[align on the requirements]] before coding. If there's still uncertainty, I [[build a quick proof of concept]] or a small slice and demo it early. It's much cheaper to change direction after two days than after two months.

questions.en: How do you handle several urgent priorities at the same time?
questions.goal: Organização e comunicação num ambiente rápido.
questions.answer: I make the trade-offs visible. I list what's on my plate, estimate the impact of each item, and [[sync up with]] the tech lead or product to agree on the order. Production issues affecting clients come first. And [[I keep people in the loop]]: if something will slip, they hear it from me early.

questions.en: What do you look for when you review someone's code?
questions.goal: Qualidade e colaboração: a vaga cita code review e testes.
questions.answer: First, correctness: does it solve the problem, and what about the edge cases? Then tests, readability and naming, and any security or data-isolation risk, which is critical in a multi-tenant system. I try to keep comments about the code, not the person, and I separate blocking issues from suggestions. And I prefer small pull requests: they get better reviews.

questions.en: How do you design a REST API that other systems depend on?
questions.goal: Os produtos de pagamento dependem da API. Querem ver cuidado com contrato e compatibilidade.
questions.answer: I treat the API as a contract. I model it around resources, version it from day one, and never break existing clients: new fields are additive. I use consistent error formats, cursor-based pagination for large lists, and idempotency keys on POST requests, so a retry never creates a duplicate. With FastAPI, the OpenAPI documentation comes for free. And authentication defines the tenant, so every request is scoped to one client.
follow_ups: How would you version the API?
What is idempotency and why does it matter here?

questions.en: When would you choose FastAPI over Django?
questions.goal: Se você conhece os trade-offs, não só a sintaxe.
questions.answer: Django is great when I need a full product quickly: ORM, migrations, admin and auth out of the box. The admin is perfect for internal operator screens. FastAPI shines for API-first services: it's async, very fast, and the type hints give me validation and documentation automatically. [[As a rule of thumb]], Django for the core product with many models, FastAPI for focused, high-throughput services.

questions.en: How would you find duplicate vendors using SQL?
questions.goal: SQL sólido: normalização, window functions, índices e similaridade.
questions.answer: First I'd normalize the key fields, for example upper case, trimmed names without punctuation, and tax IDs with digits only. For exact duplicates, I'd use a window function: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id, normalized_tax_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC), and everything with row number greater than one is a duplicate candidate. For fuzzy duplicates in PostgreSQL, I'd use the pg_trgm extension with a trigram index to compare name similarity, but only inside smaller blocks, like the same ZIP code, to avoid comparing every record with every other one.
tips: Se pedirem para escrever a query, fale enquanto escreve: 'I'm partitioning by...'

questions.en: An endpoint suddenly became slow in production. How do you investigate?
questions.goal: Método de investigação, não chute.
questions.answer: First I measure instead of guessing: logs, APM traces and which tenant or input is slow. [[Nine times out of ten]], it's the database, so I look at the slow queries and run EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Typical causes are a missing index, an N+1 query, or a query without pagination that grew with the data. I fix the root cause, add a test or an alert so it doesn't come back, and only then think about caching.

questions.en: How would you design a multi-tenant system? How do you guarantee one client never sees another client's data?
questions.goal: Requisito explícito da vaga e risco grave em pagamentos.
questions.answer: There are three common models: a shared schema with a tenant_id column, a schema per tenant, or a database per tenant. [[The trade-off is]] isolation versus cost and operational complexity. For many clients, I'd usually start with a shared schema and tenant_id on every table. Then I'd enforce isolation in layers: the tenant comes from the authentication token, never from the request body; all queries go through a base repository that filters by tenant; PostgreSQL row-level security as a safety net; and automated tests that try to read another tenant's data and must fail. I'd also watch for noisy neighbors: one big client shouldn't slow down everyone else.

questions.en: Have you worked with event-driven or message-based architectures? How do you handle failures?
questions.goal: Experiência com filas e, principalmente, se você entende entrega 'at-least-once'.
questions.answer: Yes, ((describe what you used: for example Celery with Redis or RabbitMQ, SQS...)). The key thing is that most queues deliver messages at least once, so consumers must be idempotent: processing the same message twice can't create a duplicate. I use retries with exponential backoff and a dead-letter queue for messages that keep failing, so they can be inspected and replayed. To avoid saving to the database and failing to publish the event, I use the outbox pattern. And I monitor queue depth and age, because a growing queue is an early warning.
tips: Se a sua experiência for só com Celery, diga isso. Os conceitos são os mesmos.

questions.en: A client uploads a file with two million vendor records. How do you process it?
questions.goal: Processamento assíncrono e robusto, um cenário real da vaga.
questions.answer: Not inside the HTTP request. The API stores the file in blob storage, like S3 or Azure Blob, and returns 202 Accepted with a job ID. A worker splits the file into batches and publishes them to a queue, so several workers can process in parallel. Each record is validated: good records continue, bad records go to a report with the reason, so one bad line doesn't fail the whole file. The client can follow the progress through the job status endpoint, and the processing is idempotent, so if a worker crashes we can safely resume.

questions.en: What's your testing strategy?
questions.goal: Disciplina de qualidade.
questions.answer: Mostly fast unit tests with pytest, some integration tests against a real PostgreSQL, and a few end-to-end tests for the critical flows. For matching logic specifically, I'd keep a labeled set of tricky real-world examples, like 'ACME Inc.' versus 'Acme Incorporated', and run it in CI, so any change to the rules shows exactly which matches improved or broke. And contract tests for the API, because other systems depend on it.

questions.en: What's your experience with Azure or AWS?
questions.goal: Requisito da vaga. Honestidade aqui vale mais do que fingir.
questions.answer: ((List what you really used, e.g. 'On AWS, I've used EC2, S3 and RDS for PGBA's products')). [[I haven't used]] ((Azure)) [[in production yet, but]] the concepts map directly: Blob Storage is like S3, Service Bus is like SQS and SNS, Azure Functions are like Lambda. [[I'm confident I can ramp up quickly]].
tips: Nunca diga que usou algo que não usou: a próxima pergunta vai expor isso.

questions.en: Tell me about your frontend experience. Have you worked with Angular?
questions.goal: A vaga é full-stack: telas para operadores.
questions.answer: My frontend experience is mostly React with TypeScript. ((For example, I recently built a mobile web app with React, TypeScript and Vite.)) [[I haven't used]] Angular [[professionally, but]] it's also TypeScript and components, and I'm familiar with the ideas behind it, like services and dependency injection. For this platform, I imagine screens like a review queue, where operators confirm or reject suggested matches. I'd focus on making that fast with keyboard shortcuts and showing why the system suggested each match.

questions.en: How would you deduplicate vendors coming from different clients and systems?
questions.goal: A pergunta central da vaga. Querem um processo, não uma biblioteca mágica.
questions.answer: I'd build it as a pipeline. First, standardize: names in the same case, without punctuation and legal suffixes like Inc or LLC, addresses in a standard format, tax IDs with digits only. Second, use strong identifiers first: if the tax ID or bank account matches, that's a very strong signal. Third, blocking: only compare records that share something, like the ZIP code or the first letters of the name, to avoid comparing millions of pairs. Fourth, score the candidates with fuzzy similarity on name and address, and use two thresholds: high scores are matched automatically, the gray zone goes to human review, low scores are different vendors. Finally, survivorship rules build the golden record, and I never delete the source records, so every decision is traceable and reversible. And I'd measure precision and recall on a labeled set before changing any threshold.
tips: Palavras-chave que eles esperam: standardization, blocking, scoring, thresholds, human review, golden record, survivorship, lineage, precision/recall.
follow_ups: What similarity algorithms would you use?
How do you choose the thresholds?

questions.en: What's worse in this domain: a false match or a missed match?
questions.goal: Pergunta de senioridade: entender o impacto de negócio do erro.
questions.answer: In payments, a false match is usually worse. If we merge two different vendors, money can go to the wrong company or the wrong bank account, and that's very hard to undo. A missed match creates a duplicate vendor, which is bad, but we can detect and merge it later. So I'd set a high threshold for automatic merges and send the uncertain cases to review. [[That said]], duplicates also cause real problems, like paying the same invoice twice, so I'd monitor both rates per client.

questions.en: What data-quality checks would you put in place?
questions.goal: 'Clean, trustworthy records' é o produto. Como você garante isso?
questions.answer: On ingestion: schema validation, required fields and format checks, for example tax ID length and checksum or bank routing numbers. Records that fail go to quarantine with a clear reason, instead of being silently fixed or dropped. Then checks on the dataset: volume anomalies, like a client file with half the usual rows, duplicate rate per tenant, and freshness. All of that goes to dashboards and alerts, so we find problems before the payment products do.

questions.en: How would you reconcile vendor records between our platform and a client's ERP?
questions.goal: Reconciliação entre fontes, citada como bônus na vaga.
questions.answer: I'd keep a crosswalk table that maps each source system and source ID to our master vendor ID. Then I'd compare snapshots and classify every record: matched, matched with different fields, only in the ERP, or only in our platform. Each category has an action: some are fixed automatically, others go to a report or a review queue. It runs on a schedule, it's idempotent, and it keeps history, so we can show the client what changed and when.

questions.en: How would you use AI or LLMs to help with matching?
questions.goal: Bônus da vaga: AI-assisted matching. Querem uso sensato, não hype.
questions.answer: I'd use AI where the rules struggle, not everywhere. Embeddings can help find candidate pairs that string similarity misses, like abbreviations or translated names. An LLM can act as a tie-breaker for the gray zone, returning a decision and an explanation that the operator can see. But I'd keep a human in the loop for anything that affects payments, measure it against a labeled set, and watch cost, latency and data privacy. Day to day, I also use AI coding tools ((like ...)) to move faster, always reviewing what they produce.

questions.en: A vendor's bank account changes in one of the sources. What should the platform do?
questions.goal: Consciência de risco em pagamentos (fraude por troca de dados bancários é comum).
questions.answer: I'd treat it as a high-risk change. A bank account change is a classic fraud pattern in accounts payable. So the platform shouldn't propagate it automatically: flag it, keep the previous value active, require verification, and record everything in an audit log. I'd also notify the client and alert if the same account suddenly appears on several unrelated vendors.

questions.en: Design a platform that ingests vendor data from many client firms, cleans and unifies it, and serves it to payment products through an API.
questions.goal: Visão de arquitetura de ponta a ponta. Comece perguntando, depois desenhe por camadas.
questions.answer: [[Before I start, can I ask a few questions?]] How many clients and records, how often the data changes, and how fresh it needs to be for the payment products. Then I'd split it into layers. Ingestion: clients send data by API or file upload; raw data goes to blob storage untouched, and an event starts processing. Processing: event-driven workers validate, standardize, match and merge, each step idempotent, with a dead-letter queue. Storage: PostgreSQL with tenants, source records, master vendors, match links and an audit log. Review: an operator screen for the uncertain matches. Serving: a versioned REST API for the golden records, plus events or webhooks when a vendor changes. Across everything: tenant isolation, monitoring and data-quality alerts. [[I'd start simple]] and only split into more services when the volume requires it.
tips: Fale enquanto desenha. Pergunte antes de desenhar.
Use: 'Let me start with the big picture, and then we can zoom in.'
follow_ups: How would you scale it when the volume grows ten times?
Where would you put the matching logic?

questions.en: How would you scale it if the volume grew ten times?
questions.goal: Gargalos reais e não reescrever tudo.
questions.answer: First I'd find the real bottleneck with metrics. Usually it's matching, because it grows faster than the data. So I'd make matching incremental, comparing only new or changed records, with good blocking keys and indexes. Workers scale horizontally from the queue depth, and large clients can be processed in separate partitions so they don't affect smaller ones. On the read side, read replicas and caching for the API.

questions.en: Do you have any questions for us?
questions.goal: Nunca responda 'no'. Perguntas boas mostram que você já se imagina no time.
questions.answer: Yes, a few. [[I'm curious to know]] what the platform looks like today and what the biggest pain point is. How is matching done right now: rules, machine learning, or mostly manual review? Are you on Azure or AWS, and Angular or React? [[What would success look like]] for this role in the first ninety days? And what are the next steps in the process?
tips: Escolha 3 ou 4. Anote as respostas: elas ajudam na próxima entrevista.

questions.en: Great, that's all from our side. Anything else you'd like to add?
questions.goal: Última impressão. Curto, positivo, e reforce o encaixe.
questions.answer: Just that I'm really excited about this opportunity. The problem you're solving is exactly the kind of work I enjoy, and I'd love to take ownership of it. [[Thank you for the opportunity]], [[it was great chatting with you]], and [[I look forward to hearing from you]].
